headline: Google wants to simplify online shopping with Universal Cart
summary: Google's new Universal Cart aims to streamline browsing, deal tracking, and checkout, potentially changing how we shop online.
details: Google is introducing a new feature called Universal Cart, designed to act as your personal shopping assistant across the web. The system allows users to drop items into a single cart from various platforms, including Search, Gemini, YouTube, and eventually Gmail.

This Universal Cart is built on Google Wallet and can track deals, price drops, price history, and restocks. Google's AP2 protocol is being developed to enable AI agents to complete purchases under user-approved limits, aiming to make online shopping more convenient.

The system uses a new Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) to communicate with retailers and an Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) for secure transactions. This allows Google's AI agents to assemble a cart and finalize purchases, with payments processed through tokenized Google Pay.

While offering convenience, the feature raises privacy concerns about centralizing so much purchasing power with Google. However, Google anticipates that users will appreciate the ease of avoiding account creation and form-filling.

Retailers face potential loss of site visits and merchandising opportunities as Google's agents handle discovery and checkout. Despite this, major brands like Nike, Sephora, Target, and Walmart are early adopters, pressured by competitive dynamics.
Google's move signifies a broader trend of agents handling more tasks, potentially reshaping the internet's infrastructure and user interaction with online retail.
